messages.subject: marked LGCP
parts:
Hi,

I’m trying to apply a marked LGCP model to my data but I get this error:

GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [12]
Reason    : The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge
Message   : Condition `lambda < 1.0 / lambda_lim' is not TRUE
Function  : GMRFLib_init_GMRF_approximation_store__intern
File      : approx-inference.c
Line      : 2842
RCSId     : file: approx-inference.c  hgid: 755a4114e167  date: Wed Aug 19 15:24:56 2015 +0200

I considered poisson distribution for the marks, but I did not define the exposure in this case. When I assume exposure=1, I get the same error. When I assume exposure=0, the model runs, but the estimates are not similar to what I would expect. Which value must I consider for the exposure? 
In this case, the marks have many zeros, so I have also tried to consider zeroinflatedpoisson0, but I get the same error..

Can anyone help me, please?

Thank you.
Soraia

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] marked LGCP
parts:
Hi Soraia,

Am I correct in assuming you used poisson for the points also?

I would think exposure = 1 should be the natural choice.

Can you send me
1) The code defining the model
2) The resource you used to copy-paste code from (e.g. was it the SPDE tutorial?)
3) The result$logfile, or the output with verbose=T (these are the same)

PS. The marked LGCP is quite complicated to implement, and so it would be good to check that you have implemented exactly what you wanted.

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] marked LGCP
parts:
Hi Haakon Bakka,

Thank you very much for your reply. Meantime, Elias Krainski helped me to understand that this model can be sensitive to coordinates system used. I needed to do a projection from lat and lon to utm in km. After this, the model runs and the results are similar to what I would expect. 
The code I used is

stk.pp <- inla.stack(data=list(y=cbind(y.pp.cov,NA), e=e.pp.cov,link=1), A=list(1,A.pp.cov), tag='pp',
                     effects=list(list(b0.pp=rep(1,nv+n.cov),dens.pp=densidade_pop), list(i=1:nv)))

stk.m <- inla.stack(data=list(y=cbind(NA,marcas),e=c(rep(1,nv+n.cov)),link=1), A=list(lmat.cov.marcas, 1), tag='marcas',
                    effects=list(list(j=1:nv,k=1:nv),list(b0.y=rep(1,nv+n.cov))))

j.stk <- inla.stack(stk.pp, stk.m)

jform <- y ~ 0 + b0.pp + b0.y   + 
f(i, model=spde) + f(j, copy='i', fixed=TRUE) +f(k, model=spde)

j.res <- inla(jform, family=c('poisson', 'poisson'), data=inla.stack.data(j.stk), E=inla.stack.data(j.stk)$e,
                control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(j.stk),compute=TRUE,link=1),  
              control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE,waic=TRUE),
                quantiles=c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), 
                control.results=list(return.marginals.random=F,return.marginals.predictor=F), 
                control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb"))

I followed the SPDE tutorial.

Thank you.
Best regards,
Soraia
